messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1: Multiple customer connections failing to external services from eu-west-1a. Alert group: VPC-EGRESS-ERRORS. Paging jamie (oncall).

jamie (oncall): saw the page, joining. Anyone already looked at flow logs?

maria (support): multiple tickets from customers in EU reporting outbound failures to 3rd-party APIs starting ~04:02 UTC. Correlates with svc-latency spikes.

priya (eng-net): i'm on it — checking route tables and NAT health in eu-west-1.

ben (sre): checking metrics: NAT gw-a (eu-west-1a) outbound bytes collapsed at 04:01 and connections spike 500x. NAT gw-b (1b) looks normal.

priya (eng-net): console shows NAT gw-a is "associated" but its elastic IP is in a weird state (ENI detached briefly). I see recent terraform apply on vpc-egress-routes from 03:55 by deploy-bot.

jamie (oncall): could be a route table assoc drift or NACL. priya, can you confirm route table assoc for private subnets in 1a?

priya (eng-net): checking: route-table-priv-1a currently has 0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-gw-a (id:nat-0abc). But the attachment shows target eni: eni-DETACHED (status: unavailable). There was also a NACL change at 03:58 (nacl-12345 inbound/ephemeral). logs show "deny ephemeral ports" rule added by infra-team.

ben (sre): that NACL change rings alarm bells. If ephemeral client ports blocked, TCP handshakes to external APIs fail even if NAT exists. maria any customer commonality?

maria (support): customers affected are all in eu-west-1a subnets behind the private NAT. Some using long-lived sockets that suddenly closed.

sasha (sec): who applied the NACL change? I can see the author: infra-automation (ci-runner). It was intended for hardening but the rule was too broad.

jamie (oncall): okay, triage plan: 1) revert NACL change to last-known-good, 2) reattach/replace nat-gw-a ENI or failover traffic to nat-gw-b, 3) run quick customer impact check and post status. Priya/Ben take action 1&2. Maria will draft customer blurb. Sasha, flag if rollback violates any security policy.

priya (eng-net): executing rollback now: terraform rollback NACL rule -> applying.

ops-bot: Rollback job started (job id: rb-2026-04-15-01).

ben (sre): while that's running, i'm detaching the unhealthy ENI and creating a replacement NAT gateway in 1a to preserve AZ locality. command:

```
aws ec2 allocate-address --domain vpc
aws ec2 create-nat-gateway --subnet-id subnet-priv-1a --allocation-id eipalloc-xxxxx
```

jamie (oncall): if create-nat-gateway takes too long (ETA ~2-3 mins), plan B is to update route table to point 0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-gw-b in 1b temporarily (cross-AZ). That will spike costs but restore outbound for urgent customers.

priya (eng-net): rollback finished — NACL reverted to previous rules. I can confirm ephemeral ports allowed again. Please monitor connections.

ben (sre): new NAT gw creation succeeded (nat-0efg) attached to subnet-priv-1a. Updating route table to point to the new NAT now.

priya (eng-net): route table association updated, propagation done.

maria (support): initial customer blurb draft: "We're aware of intermittent outbound failures for services in eu-west-1a. Root cause: recent network hardening change combined with transient NAT gateway ENI detachment. We have reverted the change and re-provisioned NAT; outbound connectivity has been restored for most customers. We're continuing to monitor and will update in 30 mins." Want to post?

jamie (oncall): good. post to status.redwood.ai and reply to open tickets. Add an "incident in progress" note.

sasha (sec): quick note: the NACL change originated from a automation rule that tried to block ephemeral 1024-65535 from certain subnets. That rule had a missing CIDR and matched more than intended. We'll audit the automation runbook. I approve rollback; no compliance blockers.

ben (sre): monitoring shows request success rate back to baseline in 1a. Logs show TCP handshakes restored ~04:09 UTC.

jamie (oncall): assigning follow-ups: priya to file a post-incident RFC describing the automation gap and add a safelist test; sasha to update policy so automation requires peer review for NACL changes; ben to add alerting that catches ENI detach+NACL deny patterns; maria to send customer follow-up with RCA when we have it. I'll start the incident timeline.

priya (eng-net): noted. creating a ticket now: RFC-2467 - NACL automation safety.

maria (support): posted status update and replied to 18 active tickets with an interim message. Customers acknowledging.

ops-bot: Incident channel updated: severity -> P1; status -> mitigated; duration so far -> 8 minutes.

jamie (oncall): handing off to priya for next 4 hours (oncall relief arriving). Priya, you own postmortem items. I'm going offline for a bit but reachable.

priya (eng-net): taking over. I'll keep monitoring and loop in networking infra to do a deeper root cause.

ben (sre): adding a quick synthetic test to hit a known external endpoint from eu-west-1a subnets every 30s to ensure no regression.

sasha (sec): prepping a short incident note for the monthly security review.

jamie (oncall): thanks team :thumbsup:

priya (eng-net): leaving the channel to reduce noise; will reopen if any regressions.

incident-bot: Incident P1 closed to active responders. Postmortem required within 72 hours.

maria (support): closing thread from support side — tickets will be updated after postmortem.
